Get the cori.data.ipeds variable codebook

get_ipeds_codebook.Rd

Returns documentation for every variable available via get_ipeds() and get_ipeds(). Covers the three IPEDS surveys this package harmonizes: Institutional Characteristics, Completions, and Graduation Rates, 2010 to present.

Usage

get_ipeds_codebook()

Value

A data frame with columns: variable, raw_variable, label, unit, survey, level, notes, codes. raw_variable is the original NCES column name, as stored in the data_raw layer on S3; it is empty for derived county-level variables. codes decodes the categorical variables – a "1 = Public; 2 = Private not-for-profit" string – and is empty for the rest.

Details

Use level to separate the two output levels: "institution" variables appear in get_ipeds()'s institution-level output, "county" variables in get_ipeds()'s tidy output, and "both" marks the join keys present in every table.

notes records vintage caveats – which years a variable covers, NCES column renames, and taxonomy changes – so cross-year comparability is documented alongside the variable rather than in separate prose.

Much of IPEDS is categorical, and the institution-level output returns those columns as the bare integers NCES publishes. codes carries the value labels for them, transcribed from the NCES data dictionary workbooks, so a sector_code of 4 can be resolved without leaving the package. Only codes that actually occur in this package's output are listed. NCES sentinel values (-1, -2, -3) are converted to NA during the ETL and so do not appear.

See also

get_ipeds(), get_ipeds()

Examples

cb <- get_ipeds_codebook()

# County-level variables only
cb[cb$level == "county", c("variable", "label", "unit")]
#>                   variable                                 label
